newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: China mulls buying term Alaskan North Slope crude.
newsitem.headline: China mulls buying term Alaskan North Slope crude.

text.p: China is looking to import term Alaskan North Slope (ANS) crude oil in the near future, a trader close to China's state-owned China International United Petroleum and Chemicals Co Ltd (Unipec) said on Monday.

"We have taken two ANS cargoes and we are quite happy with it and we would possibly sign a term contract in the near future, depending on price," the trader told Reuters on the sidelines of an oil conference.
He said China bought on a spot basis two 230,000 barrels cargoes of ANS for end December 1996 and January 1997 delivery and Chinese refineries had no problem refining the crude.
"It is similar to Oman crude, we have no problems with it," the crude trader said.
Alaskan crude has an American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity of 27.9 degree and sulphur content of 0.895 percent. Oman has an API of 35.3 degrees and sulphur content of 0.851 percent.
The trader said a Chinese oil team, including Unipec, visited Alaska in March to do a feasibility study on importing ANS.
He said Unipec was in contact with British Petroleum to buy more ANS on a spot basis.
BP is a major equity holder in Alaskan oil fields and started exports to Asia after the United States lifted a 21-year ban last year.
In Asia, South Korea's LG-Caltex Oil Corp is the largest long-term buyer of ANS, importing 30,000 barrels per day from BP in a deal which became effective last December.
Taiwan and Japan are also buyers of the crude.
